researchUpdates.title: Integrated Performance Assessment of Sustainable One-Part Geopolymer Seawater Sea-Sand Concrete Reinforced with Hybrid Polypropylene Fibers
researchUpdates.authors: Alaa M. Mehriz, Mariam F. Ghazy, Omar H. Khalifa and Eslam Arafa
researchUpdates.summary: An experimental assessment combines a dry, one-part geopolymer binder with seawater and sea sand, then examines hybrid polypropylene-fiber reinforcement across mechanical, durability and environmental performance.
highlights: The design addresses freshwater and natural-sand substitution together with fiber reinforcement in one formulation, rather than evaluating either change in isolation.

Its reported performance belongs to the tested binder, marine materials and hybrid-fiber combination; it should not be transferred to other seawater sources, activators or fiber blends without validation.
researchUpdates.access: Publisher-indexed abstract and PDF metadata only because the direct article page returned HTTP 429 during review. Full mixture proportions, specimen program, fiber dosages, reported ages, statistical uncertainty and life-cycle boundaries were not independently audited. No strength at an unreported age or independent replication is claimed.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary publisher-indexed metadata and PDF search evidence; no abstract text, publisher highlights, figures, tables or full-paper passages were reproduced

journalArticle.title: Substitution boundaries belong to the mixture
journalArticle.summary: A marine-material geopolymer study shows why water source, aggregate source and fiber system must travel together with performance claims.
paragraphs: Replacing freshwater and natural sand with seawater and sea sand changes ionic exposure and aggregate conditions at the same time that hybrid polypropylene fibers alter cracking behavior. These are coupled variables, not interchangeable sustainability labels.

For the formulation database, preserve seawater chemistry, sea-sand grading and chloride content, dry-activator composition, fiber types and dosages, curing, test age and response type. This single experimental program does not validate every marine-source material or supply unreported strength timelines.
